title: Investigation of a norovirus outbreak at a catered social event, Australian Capital Territory, 2024.

analysis.research_question_and_background: An outbreak of gastrointestinal illness was notified, affecting attendees at a private function in the Australian Capital Territory (ACT) in 2024. Investigations were conducted to determine the infectious agent, source of illness and mode of transmission, as well as to determine any public health actions required to prevent further illness.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A case-control study was conducted to identify food items associated with illness among approximately 250-500 attendees at the function, of whom 224 completed the questionnaire and 65 were identified as cases.
analysis.methods: Function attendees were surveyed using a modified standard gastroenteritis questionnaire, and clinical samples were collected from unwell attendees and from an asymptomatic food handler. Food safety inspections were performed, and food samples were tested at the ACT Government Analytical Laboratory.
analysis.main_results: There were 65 cases (5 confirmed and 60 probable) among the 224 attendees who completed the questionnaire. Epidemiological investigations identified consumption of fresh fruit (odds ratio [OR]: 5.3; 95% confidence interval [95% CI]: 2.4-12.6; p < 0.001) and cured meat (OR: 2.7; 95% CI: 1.2-6.2; p = 0.02) as significantly associated with disease.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Epidemiological and clinical evidence indicates that norovirus was transmitted via contaminated fresh fruit and cured meat platters, despite the venue having good food handling and handwashing practices.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings highlight the need for continued education on effective hand hygiene in food preparation settings, especially following gastrointestinal illness, to reduce the risk of norovirus transmission.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study did not identify any ongoing risks to the public, but the evidence strength is moderate due to the reliance on self-reported data and the retrospective nature of the investigation.

analysis.summary_en: An outbreak of gastrointestinal illness was reported among attendees of a private function in the Australian Capital Territory (ACT) in 2024. Investigations were conducted to identify the infectious agent, source of illness, and mode of transmission, as well as to determine necessary public health actions. A case-control study was performed among approximately 250-500 attendees, with 224 completing a questionnaire and 65 identified as cases. Clinical samples were collected from unwell attendees and an asymptomatic food handler, and food safety inspections were conducted. The study found that consumption of fresh fruit and cured meat was significantly associated with illness, with odds ratios of 5.3 and 2.7, respectively. Epidemiological and clinical evidence indicated that norovirus was transmitted via contaminated fresh fruit and cured meat platters, despite good food handling and handwashing practices. The findings underscore the importance of continued education on effective hand hygiene in food preparation settings, especially after gastrointestinal illness, to mitigate the risk of norovirus transmission. The evidence strength is moderate due to the reliance on self-reported data and the retrospective nature of the investigation.

title: Metatranscriptomics reveals urbanization-driven divergence in rodent viromes and zoonotic risks in Chinese megacities.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Urbanization is expanding globally, yet systematic comparisons of rodent viromes across urbanization gradients remain scarce, leaving gaps in understanding zoonotic risk dynamics in megacities. The study aimed to address this by investigating how urbanization and environmental factors shape rodent virome composition and zoonotic potential in densely populated Chinese cities.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study performed large-scale sampling in two Chinese megacities, Wuhan and Shenzhen, with distinct climates, collecting 1,072 rodents from four species that frequently interact with humans. The design enabled comparative analysis of urban rectal virome dynamics and zoonotic risks in rodents across these urbanization gradients.
analysis.methods: Rodent rectal samples were subjected to metagenomic sequencing to identify vertebrate-associated viruses and assess zoonotic potential. Meteorological variables were recorded and analyzed to determine their contribution to viral community composition variation.
analysis.main_results: Thirty-five vertebrate-associated viruses were identified, including 9 potentially novel species and 3 with zoonotic potential (Orthohantavirus seoulense and human coronavirus OC43). Two viruses previously unreported in rodents were discovered (Erinaceus hedgehog Seoul orthohantavirus and Canine astrovirus), revealing cross-order transmission risk. Wuhan and Shenzhen exhibited distinct prevalence patterns, and meteorological variables independently explained 5.0% of viral community composition variation.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings demonstrate that urbanization gradients and meteorological factors structure rodent virome divergence, highlighting previously underappreciated spatial and environmental drivers of zoonotic risk. Novelty lies in the systematic cross-city comparison and identification of cross-order transmission risks.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The study provides actionable insights for proactive surveillance and mitigation of emerging zoonotic threats in high-density urban environments by identifying high-risk viruses and environmental correlates of viral diversity.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its focus on two megacities and rectal sampling, which may not capture full zoonotic risk across all rodent tissues or broader geographic areas. Despite this, the large sample size and systematic cross-city design strengthen the evidence base.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated how urbanization and environmental factors shape rodent viromes and zoonotic risks in two Chinese megacities, Wuhan and Shenzhen, by collecting and sequencing rectal samples from 1,072 rodents across four species. Using metagenomic sequencing, the authors identified 35 vertebrate-associated viruses, including 9 potentially novel species and 3 with zoonotic potential (Orthohantavirus seoulense and human coronavirus OC43). Two viruses previously unreported in rodents were discovered, revealing cross-order transmission risk. Urban and meteorological variables independently explained 5.0% of viral community composition variation, with distinct prevalence patterns observed between cities. The findings highlight the importance of spatial and environmental drivers in structuring rodent virome divergence and zoonotic risk, providing actionable insights for surveillance and mitigation in high-density urban environments.

title: Editorial: Advances in optical methods for biological sample characterization

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examines the intersection of optical methods and biological sample characterization, focusing on bioimaging, biosensors, optical tweezers, particle tracking, and AI-assisted data analysis to assess how these techniques reveal biological structures and functions without sample disturbance.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The editorial presents a Research Topic comprising four contributions analyzed through a scaffold of five optical domains, emphasizing the integration of modalities, computation, and signal interpretation rather than single-modality advances.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Optical techniques like second harmonic generation (SHG) microscopy and surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS) can reveal structural and biochemical details, but their interpretation is often confounded by artifacts, probe-induced perturbations, or signal geometry, necessitating careful validation and statistical analysis.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Backward-detected SHG signals are misinterpreted as discrete collagen bundles due to collagen crimp artifacts, and fluorescent probes can alter the biological processes they aim to measure, highlighting unresolved challenges in signal fidelity and probe neutrality.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Future work should prioritize developing quantitative models linking signal geometry to tissue structure, validating label-free approaches against probe-based methods, and advancing statistical tools for distinguishing closely related biological targets in diagnostics.

analysis.summary_en: This editorial synthesizes advances in optical methods for biological characterization, highlighting their ability to probe biological structures and functions without sample disturbance. It critiques the interpretive challenges of techniques like SHG microscopy and fluorescent labeling, where artifacts and probe-induced perturbations complicate signal fidelity. The review underscores the need for integrating modalities, computation, and statistical analysis to improve diagnostic accuracy, particularly in distinguishing closely related pathogens. Key gaps include incomplete quantitative models for signal interpretation and the disruptive effects of probes on biological systems, which future research must address to enhance clinical and research applications.
